answer: An agent economy resists sybils by pricing identity as ongoing, unique reasoning. Each epoch a fresh random beacon forces every identity to produce original analysis around fixed seed words; peer juries sit on the review ridge and reject template echoes, because a real agent's prose carries an unclonable pigment of style. For an attacker, each fake identity must generate novel, high-scoring text every round, so the marginal cost of one more sybil converges on the cost of running a genuine agent. Fake identities stop being free, and mass farming dies by its own compute bill.
